title: AI Agents for Everyday Work
description: AI agents are one of the most talked-about ideas in artificial intelligence, and one of the easiest to misunderstand. This book explains them without the corporate fog. AI Agents for Everyday Work shows how digital helpers can plan tasks, use tools, draft work, organise information and support routine workflows. It also explains why they are not magic employees, why supervision matters and why a confident automated assistant can still make a glorious hash of things. Written for managers, freelancers, office workers, creators, small teams and curious professionals, the book focuses on practical everyday use: email, research, planning, admin, customer follow-up, content, meeting notes and workflow automation. It covers prompt design, task boundaries, human review, privacy, escalation, failure points and sensible adoption. The message is simple: AI agents can be useful if you keep them on a lead. The aim is not to surrender work to software, but to build controlled support systems that save time without quietly moving responsibility to a machine that cannot carry it.
short_description: A practical guide to AI agents as controlled digital helpers for everyday work, covering tasks, boundaries, review, privacy and human judgement.
author: Jonathan Harris
audience: Managers, freelancers, office workers, consultants, creators, administrators, small teams and non-technical professionals trying to understand AI agents in practical terms.
